_note: MULTIQ-1108 (owner 2026-11-08: 'Sometimes, people pose multi-question or multi-part question prompts. VD needs to be able to handle both.'). Plan: work/MULTIQ-1108/plan.md (root workspace). vera/multi_question.py splits a prompt into separate questions from its grammatical structure only: question marks, sentence boundaries followed by an interrogative-led clause, and conjoined interrogative clauses with their own auxiliary verb. The word sets below are closed grammatical classes (interrogatives, auxiliaries, leading conjunctions, pronouns), not topic, name or keyword lists. A multi-PART question (one question with several sides or facets, vera.subquery) is never split; it is only recorded.
_mode_note: MULTIQ-1109. Owner 2026-11-08, verbatim: "Sometimes, people pose multi-question or multi-part question prompts. VD needs to be able to handle both." That is a capability requirement, so the shipped default is on. off = no code runs (byte-identical to before; the kill switch); shadow = the split is computed and recorded in the request trace as counts only, nothing user-visible changes; on = each question is routed and answered, or refused, on its own and the page shows one section per question. Only a prompt that holds 2+ questions is affected; a single question runs the unchanged path. Quota (reconciles SIX-1109): each question is its own research unit, one acquisition job per question, an equal share (max_docs_per_prompt // n) of the per-prompt new-document ceiling, one shared request deadline.
_max_questions_calibration_note: PROVISIONAL, UNCALIBRATED (no live multi-question traffic has been measured). Reason: the non-stream path has one 180 s request budget and one acquisition-backed question needs up to 125 s, so more than about one acquisition question per request cannot finish there (later questions say so via the deadline status); the live stream path has no deadline (OD-1031-NODEADLINE), so latency there is bounded by stream_rounds_per_question (searches per question, inline_acquire._extra_rounds). Each question is one acquisition job (acq_rounds_one_job) against jobs_per_hour 120 (OD-1109-QUOTA) and jobs_per_day (180 on this branch; 2000 once BATCH3-1109 ships), so 3 questions cost 3 jobs. The per-prompt ceiling max_docs_per_prompt 31 is shared equally (31 // n); a question keeps a share of at least the round target 6, so at most 31 // 6 = 5 questions are answered whatever this cap says: the rest are listed to ask separately (code guard in _answer_parts). Data that would change it: the multiq split counts (parts, over_cap), round_cap events and per-part latency in two weeks of request traces.
_subordinators_note: Closed grammatical class (subordinating conjunctions). A word of this class, or an interrogative, that is not the first word of the left clause makes the right clause part of the same question ('when it rains and is cold', 'between what is legal and what is ethical').
_f1_note: MULTIQ-1109 F1 (closed grammatical classes). A clause led by an adverbial interrogative with no auxiliary within aux_window ('When it rains') is a subordinate clause, so the clause after it never splits off. A right clause whose comma-set tail starts with an infinitive marker ('is it painful, to get a tattoo removed?') shares that tail with the clause before it, so no split.
_stream_rounds_per_question_note: MULTIQ-1109 F3. PROVISIONAL, UNCALIBRATED. The bound is on SEARCHES per question (round 0 plus query-variant rounds) inside vera/inline_acquire.py _extra_rounds, set per question through inline_acquire.ROUND_CAP. It applies only on the streamed path (no request deadline, OD-1031-NODEADLINE) and only to a question of a multi-question prompt; a single question and the non-stream path (bounded by the shared 180 s deadline) are unchanged. It is checked after the met / ceiling / stop checks, so a question that reached its target never counts as cut. When the cap ends a search early the stop is round_cap and the question's answer carries cut_text. Total searches for a prompt are at most n x this value. Data that would change it: round_cap trace events and per-question latency in request traces.
cut_text: The search for new documents for question {n} was stopped early so that every question gets a fair share of the time.
_aux_window_note: Grammar bound, not a decision threshold on data: inside one sentence, a clause after ', and' / '; ' / ' and ' counts as its own question only when it starts with an auxiliary, or with an interrogative followed by an auxiliary within this many words ('and what are their side effects', 'and how much does it cost'). 'pros and cons', 'safe and effective', 'and what about cost' never split. Change only if the offline eval set shows a conjoined question it misses.
over_cap_text: Not answered in this request (ask separately):
same_reason_text: Not answered, for the same reason as question {n}.
